sources.title: Human History Map, modern civilization index
sources.note: Repository index checked directly: id palestine, alias West Bank and Gaza, generated from Natural Earth, indexed from 2020 with an open lifetime. Local geometry inspection found one nine-vertex polygon with bbox 34.927,31.353 to 35.546,32.533; it depicts a coarse West Bank only and omits Gaza.

sources.title: UN Secretary-General, Status of Palestine in the United Nations
sources.note: Original Secretary-General report checked, paragraphs 1-2: General Assembly resolution 67/19 accorded Palestine non-member observer State status in 2012; the Secretariat thereafter treated it in that category. This is UN status, not a finding that occupation, borders or effective control were resolved.

sources.title: United Nations, History of the Question of Palestine
sources.note: UN historical chronology checked for the British Mandate, 1947 plan, 1948 displacement and territorial control, 1967 occupation, Oslo process, Palestinian Authority, 2005 withdrawal from Gaza and 2007 Hamas takeover. The page is an institutional synthesis and the card avoids treating a proposed partition map as an implemented border.

sources.title: UN General Assembly resolution 43/177, Question of Palestine
sources.note: Official multilingual resolution checked: the Assembly acknowledged the 15 November 1988 proclamation of the State of Palestine and decided to use the designation Palestine in place of PLO in the UN system, without prejudicing PLO observer status and functions.

sources.title: UN Peacemaker, Declaration of Principles on Interim Self-Government Arrangements, 13 September 1993
sources.note: Official deposited agreement checked: it created an interim self-government framework while reserving Jerusalem, refugees, settlements, security arrangements, borders and other issues for permanent-status negotiations. It did not settle sovereignty or final boundaries.

sources.title: UN General Assembly resolution ES-10/23, Admission of new Members, 10 May 2024
sources.note: Original resolution checked: the Assembly determined Palestine qualified for membership, asked the Security Council to reconsider, and granted additional participation modalities from the 79th session. The annex expressly withholds a General Assembly vote and candidature to UN organs; full membership was not conferred.

sources.title: International Court of Justice, Advisory Opinion on the Occupied Palestinian Territory, 19 July 2024
sources.note: Official advisory opinion checked, summary and operative conclusions: West Bank and East Jerusalem are occupied; obligations for Gaza correspond to the degree of effective control; occupation transfers no sovereignty; Israel is not entitled to sovereignty in any part of the occupied territory by virtue of occupation; the continued presence was found unlawful. Advisory, not a bilateral border award.

sources.title: UN General Assembly resolution 67/19, official Arabic edition
sources.note: Original Arabic edition checked for the written form دولة فلسطين and the references to the 1988 declaration and a sovereign State of Palestine. Translation and scholarly transliteration in the card are editorial; this is Modern Standard Arabic in an official legal document, not a transcription of spoken Palestinian Arabic.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Ancient Jericho/Tell es-Sultan
sources.note: Full UNESCO property entry checked: deposits from about 10,500 BCE, major permanent settlement by the ninth to eighth millennium BCE, spring, ditch, wall and tower, 29 occupation phases, Bronze Age planning and fortifications, inscription in 2023. Ancient inhabitants are not relabelled citizens of a modern state.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Palestine: Land of Olives and Vines - Battir
sources.note: Full UNESCO property entry checked: stone terraces, spring-fed channels, family water-sharing by timed rotation, continued agricultural use, community management and inscription in danger. Claims that every terrace is ancient are avoided because UNESCO evaluation noted dating limits.

sources.title: UNESCO, The art of embroidery in Palestine
sources.note: UNESCO 2021 intangible-heritage entry checked: symbols, colours, regional and social information, thob construction, household gatherings, mother-to-daughter learning, training courses and income. Described as a documented living practice without claiming every woman participates.

sources.title: UNESCO, Dabkeh, traditional dance in Palestine
sources.note: UNESCO 2023 entry checked: eleven dancers regardless of gender, line or semicircle, linked hands and shoulders, jumping and footwork, family yards, weddings and graduations, local-dialect songs and learning by participation and imitation.

sources.title: UNESCO, Tradition of Nabulsi soap making in Palestine
sources.note: UNESCO 2024 entry checked: olive oil, water and lye; family stamp; one-year storage; adults and children cut and pack; household and workshop transmission; income and gift giving. The playful sentence in the card is clearly editorial and does not alter the process.

sources.title: UNICEF State of Palestine, Gaza children need support to get back to learning, 27 January 2026
sources.note: Dated UNICEF field account checked: around 700,000 school-age children, 92 per cent of schools needing major rehabilitation or reconstruction, 135,462 children in 111 temporary learning spaces, subjects taught, safety lessons, displacement and student voices. Figures are dated January 2026, not timeless totals.

sources.title: WHO, Women at the frontline of Gaza polio response, 8 March 2026
sources.note: Dated WHO account checked: wastewater detection in July 2024, a confirmed case in an unvaccinated infant, Ministry of Health leadership with WHO and partners, mass campaigns, and four women health workers profiled. The card treats this as a public-health achievement under extreme constraints, not proof the wider health system is intact.

sources.title: UNICEF State of Palestine, Humanitarian Situation Update at mid-year 2026, 17 July 2026
sources.note: Dated report checked: 1.9 of 2.1 million displaced, severe service constraints, 82 per cent of families water insecure, up to 70 per cent unable to access six litres per person per day, nearly 90 per cent of water and sanitation infrastructure damaged or destroyed, limited latrines and disrupted waste/sludge handling. These are July 2026 estimates for Gaza, not all Palestinians.

sources.title: Human History Map, historical-basemaps civilization index
sources.note: Repository index checked directly: Western Sahara begins circa 1945, remains open and aliases include SADR. Six decoded full-territory single polygons cover 1945-2100. Five historical shapes repeat nearly exactly; the 2020 shape changes modestly. None encodes the berm, control zones, mines or refugee camps.

sources.title: United Nations and Decolonization, Western Sahara
sources.note: Official UN status page checked: listed as a Non-Self-Governing Territory since 1963 after Spain transmitted information on Spanish Sahara; Spain reported ending its presence in 1976. The administering-power field is blank. This page does not recognize the atlas polygon as a settled sovereign border.

sources.title: International Court of Justice, Western Sahara Advisory Opinion, 16 October 1975
sources.note: Official opinion checked, especially paragraphs 80-83 and 162: at colonization the territory was inhabited by socially and politically organized peoples and was not terra nullius; some legal ties of allegiance and land-use ties existed, but the evidence did not establish territorial sovereignty by Morocco or the Mauritanian entity or displace self-determination through free and genuine expression.

sources.title: UN Legal Counsel, letter on the status and natural resources of Western Sahara, S/2002/161
sources.note: Original legal opinion checked, paragraphs 5-8 and 24-25: Madrid Agreement transferred administrative responsibilities to a temporary administration but not sovereignty or administering-power status; Spain withdrew in 1976, Mauritania in 1979; Morocco administered the Territory but is not listed by the UN as administering Power; resource activity must respect the interests and wishes of the people.

sources.title: UN Secretariat, Western Sahara working paper, A/AC.109/2026/17, 13 January 2026
sources.note: Original 2026 Secretariat working paper checked: competing Moroccan and Frente POLISARIO positions are attributed, activities west and east of the berm are distinguished, low-intensity hostilities and UN consultations are reported, refugee conditions and mine action are dated, and resolution 2797 is summarized. Reporting positions does not endorse them.

sources.title: United Nations Peacekeeping, MINURSO Fact Sheet
sources.note: Official mission fact sheet checked: established April 1991 for settlement proposals and ceasefire; ongoing monitoring, investigation and tension reduction; ceasefire breakdown in 2020; continuing deployment. The original referendum has not occurred.

sources.title: UN Secretary-General, Situation concerning Western Sahara, S/2025/612, 30 September 2025
sources.note: Original report checked, especially paras. 9-17: Moroccan authorities and Royal Moroccan Army activity west of the berm, Frente POLISARIO reports and activity around or east of it, MINURSO verification limits, and low-intensity incidents. Parties’ claims remain attributed; operational zones are not described as lawful sovereign borders.

sources.title: UN Security Council resolution 2797 (2025), 31 October 2025
sources.note: Original resolution and official record checked: mandate extended to 31 October 2026; talks are to take Morocco’s autonomy proposal as a basis; a final solution must be mutually acceptable and provide for self-determination. It neither records an agreed settlement nor removes Western Sahara from the UN decolonization list.

sources.title: African Union, Member States of the AU
sources.note: Official membership list checked: Sahrawi Republic is listed with accession on 22 February 1982. AU membership is reported as institutional recognition by that organization, not as universal recognition or proof that SADR effectively controls the atlas polygon.

sources.title: Pan-African Parliament, Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic member profile
sources.note: Official African Union organ profile checked for the SADR name, 27 February 1976 independence/proclamation date used by the organization and 22 February 1982 OAU/AU accession. The profile records the AU position; it is not treated as universal recognition or effective control.

sources.title: UNICEF Algeria, Humanitarian response for Sahrawi refugee children and their families
sources.note: Full UNICEF programme page checked: five camps near Tindouf in Algeria; community-run schooling and dated 2023 enrolment; 82 per cent female education personnel; learning limits; midwife and community-health-worker training; maternal, child, immunization and nutrition work. Camps are outside the mapped territory and figures are explicitly dated.

sources.title: UNHCR Global Focus, Education in the Sahrawi refugee camps
sources.note: UNHCR operational education page checked: Sahrawi education department leads camp schools, refugees implement services, Algerian curriculum is used, most secondary students leave families to study elsewhere in Algeria, and one Spanish-language secondary school operates near Smara camp. This describes refugee-camp education outside Western Sahara.

sources.title: UN Algeria, Inter-Agency Sahrawi Refugees Response Plan 2024-2025
sources.note: Original response plan checked, WASH section: in 2022 only Dakhla camp met 20 litres per person per day; 51 per cent network and 49 per cent truck distribution; maintained landfills, plastic-recycling initiative, planned water networks, household waste collection and WASH facilities at schools and clinics. Plans are not described as completed outcomes.

sources.title: UN Algeria, Sahrawi Refugee Response Plan one-year report for 2024, published May 2025
sources.note: Original inter-agency report checked: 2024 measles, whooping cough, varicella and hepatitis A outbreaks strained the camp health system despite vaccination gains; medicine, staffing and operational shortages persisted. Publication in May 2025 is distinguished from the 2024 reporting year.

sources.title: UNHCR, Exiled as a child, Sahrawi grandmother still longs for home
sources.note: UNHCR profile checked: one family divided daily life between a mud-brick house and traditional tent used for sleeping, eating, tea and receiving guests; tent weaving and repair skills; long displacement and funding limits. One household illustrates practice and memory, not every Sahrawi family.

sources.title: UNICEF Algeria, Children telling their stories through photography, 2025
sources.note: UNICEF exhibition page and PDF checked: five-day workshop, 20 Sahrawi refugee children from five camps, equal girls and boys, first camera use for many, self-chosen subjects and captions, and a September 2025 camp exhibition. The card does not generalize 20 participants to all children.

sources.title: United Nations terminology record, Western Sahara
sources.note: Official UN multilingual terminology record checked: preferred English term Western Sahara and Arabic الصحراء الغربية. The card supplies an editorial transliteration and identifies this as Modern Standard Arabic terminology, not an everyday Hassaniya sentence or a sovereignty decision.

sources.title: UNHCR, Restoring self-reliance among Sahrawi refugees in Algeria
sources.note: UNHCR profile checked: a Sahrawi youth speaks Hassaniya, described as an Arabic dialect widely spoken in Western Sahara and Mauritania, plus Arabic, English, Spanish and German; camp schooling and employment constraints. A multilingual individual is an example, not a population statistic.

sources.title: UN Secretary-General, Question of Western Sahara, A/80/290, 29 July 2025
sources.note: Original report checked, paragraphs 19-21: from 1 July 2024 through 30 June 2025 MINURSO mine action released 1,385,558 square metres and found and destroyed 335 explosive-ordnance items; aid cuts affected food, education, water, sanitation, hygiene and nutrition in five camps. Results are dated and do not mean the territory is mine-free.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Modern State of Palestine only; do not merge with Mandatory Palestine, ancient Philistines, kingdoms of Israel/Judah, Roman/Byzantine provinces or every society in the same land. Indexed 2020-open from Natural Earth. The only geometry is a nine-vertex polygon with bbox 34.927,31.353 to 35.546,32.533: a coarse West Bank shape that omits Gaza despite the alias West Bank and Gaza. It does not represent East Jerusalem, Oslo Areas A/B/C, occupation, settlements, the separation barrier, current front lines or internationally agreed final borders. Non-member observer State status, recognition by states, occupation, sovereignty claim and effective administration are kept distinct. No invented fall or successor.

Territory and Sahrawi people under unresolved decolonization; the alias Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic is not treated as settled identity. Indexed circa 1945-open. Six full-territory single polygons cover 1945-1960, 1960-1994, 1994-2000, 2000-2010, 2010-2020 and 2020-2100; historical outlines repeat nearly exactly and the modern outline changes slightly. They omit the berm, de facto Moroccan administration west of it, Polisario operation east of it, mines and refugee camps near Tindouf in Algeria. UN Non-Self-Governing status, Moroccan sovereignty/autonomy claim, SADR/Polisario independence claim and AU membership, and physical control are distinct. No border settlement, referendum result, fall or successor is inferred.
